issues.description: Constructor signature for StockIngredient is inconsistent: the problem statement (UML) and the solution expect a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template repository only provides StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch will prevent students from instantiating StockIngredient using the expected three-argument constructor (e.g., in acceptSupplyDelivery or examples in Main) and will block compilation or confuse students about which constructor to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) to the template StockIngredient class (or provide an overload that delegates to the existing constructor) so it matches the UML and the solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to require the four-argument constructor, but adding the three-argument overload to the template is the least disruptive fix.

issues.description: Constructor signature for the StockIngredient class differs between the problem statement/solution and the template. The problem diagram and the solution expect a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), while the template provides only StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch forces students to discover an unexpected constructor parameter (strictValidation) or to change the template class, creating unnecessary confusion and potential compilation errors when implementing SealSaloon methods that create new StockIngredient instances.
issues.suggestedFix: Add or restore a constructor with the signature StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template StockIngredient class (for example, by overloading the existing constructor and delegating to it). This aligns the template with the problem diagram and the solution so students can instantiate StockIngredient(name, price, quantity) as expected.
